column1: # Closed operational mode table for /usr/local/libexec/ta-op.
# ONE source of truth, read by two consumers:
#   - scripts/check_drop_first_exec.py (the repo gate: which modes are known)
#   - deploy/native/ta_op.c            (the runtime: what each mode execs)
# tests/test_ta_op_modes.py asserts the two agree exactly. There is no
# generator: a parity test over one declarative file is less machinery than
# a codegen step, and it fails just as loudly.
# Columns: mode <TAB> argc <TAB> kind <TAB> argv
#   argc  total argv count the wrapper accepts for this mode (2, or 3 when the
#         mode takes exactly one validated operand).
#   kind  builtin = handled in-wrapper after the drop, no exec at all
#         exec    = execv of the fixed absolute argv below, after the drop
#   argv  |-separated argv elements, compile-time constant. NO mode accepts a
#         caller-supplied executable, path, interpreter flag or shell string.
#         `printenv` is the only mode with an operand and it is a single
#         environment NAME matched against ^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*$ post-drop.
# Every row preserves the argv a real caller runs today; this table is a
# migration of existing operations, never a new capability.
version
env-summary
pulse
canary
printenv
claude-keepalive
codex-keepalive
bwrap-oracle
